title: Applying deep learning to iterative screening of medium-sized molecules for protein-protein interaction-targeted drug discovery.
authors: Shimizu, Yugo; Yonezawa, Tomoki; Bao, Yu; Sakamoto, Junichi; Yokogawa, Mariko; Furuya, Toshio; Osawa, Masanori; Ikeda, Kazuyoshi
one_liner_zh: 该文用深度学习迭代筛选中等尺寸分子靶向蛋白-蛋白相互作用（Keap1/Nrf2），不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，仅方法上可部分借鉴。
abstract: We combined a library of medium-sized molecules with iterative screening using multiple machine learning algorithms that were ligand-based, which resulted in a large increase of the hit rate against a protein-protein interaction target. This was demonstrated by inhibition assays using a PPI target, Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Keap1/Nrf2), and a deep neural network model based on the first-round assay data showed a highest hit rate of 27.3%. Using the models, we identified novel active and non-flat compounds far from public datasets, expanding the chemical space.
abstract_zh: 我们将中等大小分子库与基于配体的多种机器学习算法迭代筛选相结合，显著提高了针对蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用靶标的命中率。这通过使用PPI靶标Kelch样ECH相关蛋白1/核因子红细胞2相关因子2（Keap1/Nrf2）的抑制实验得到验证，基于第一轮实验数据的深度神经网络模型显示出最高命中率达27.3%。利用这些模型，我们识别出远离公共数据集的新型活性且非平面化合物，扩展了化学空间。
